summary: Tested Paid By filter fix in Procurement page Purchase History tab. All tests passed. The fix correctly filters procurements by employee name as fallback for legacy data that has paid_by name but no paid_by_employee_id.
passed_tests: 1. Paid By dropdown shows all employees who have ever paid: All, Company, Devendra Shukla, Ankush Kharat
2. Filter by 'Devendra Shukla' shows 29 results (matches expected count)
5. Clear Filters button resets Paid By filter to empty/All
6. After Clear Filters, all 298 purchases are shown
7. Filtered results show procurements from multiple farmers (Riva Vegetable, Samsuddin, Shewalwadi Market) where Devendra Shukla paid
8. Legacy data support: Filter matches by employee name (not just employee ID)
critical_code_review_comments: Frontend Procurement.js lines 485-525: Filter logic correctly handles both pseudo-IDs (name:XYZ) and real employee IDs
Frontend Procurement.js lines 383-427: loadPaidByEmployees function correctly extracts employees from both procurement-level AND individual payments
Frontend Procurement.js lines 313-349: loadData function correctly builds paidByEmployees list with name-based pseudo-IDs for legacy data
The fix uses Map keyed by employee name to combine entries with/without ID, preferring real IDs over pseudo-IDs
seed_data_creation: Used existing procurement data - 298 procurements in date range 2026-05-01 to 2026-06-04
context_for_next_testing_agent: Paid By filter fix fully tested and working. Key implementation: 1) Filter supports both real employee IDs and pseudo-IDs (name:XYZ) for legacy data, 2) Filter matches by employee name as fallback when paid_by_employee_id is NULL, 3) Dropdown shows all employees who have ever paid from last 6 months of data. Test date range: 2026-05-01 to 2026-06-04. Expected results: Devendra Shukla=29, Ankush Kharat=17, Company=133, Total=298.
